text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today after falling sharply over the past two weeks, likely driven by relief following potential U.S.-Iran negotiations reported on October 31st. That development could ease concerns about oil supply disruption—the company's refining margins benefit when crude oil prices remain elevated relative to fuel prices, and geopolitical uncertainty pushing oil to $123/barrel globally had weighed on near-term outlook. The stock had dropped 7% in the two weeks prior, suggesting investors were bracing for worse news on that front.

The bounce also fits a broader pattern: Big Oil earnings are about to be reported, and while there's caution in the air about forward guidance, refining operations have been particularly profitable lately. U.S. refineries are running at 92.8% capacity and gasoline stocks remain relatively tight at 209 million barrels, conditions that historically support refiner margins—which is exactly what the commentary about surging refining earnings reflects.
